channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Regional law firm facing data breach class action
item.description: A Rhode Island class action alleges a multistate law firm failed to safeguard personal data after a 2024 cybersecurity breach affecting thousands.

item.title: Commercial – Intra-enterprise doctrine – Chapter 93A
item.description: Where a defendant has moved to dismiss a G.L.c. 93A claim, that motion should be denied because the intra-enterprise doctrine does not preclude the plaintiff’s Chapter 93A claim.

item.title: Habeas corpus – SDP – Commitment
item.description: Where a petitioner challenged his civil commitment under G.L.c. 123A on the ground that no qualified examiner opined that he was a sexually dangerous person, a Superior Court order granting habeas corpus relief should be vacated because the petitioner had an alternative avenue to challenge his civil commitment.

item.title: Criminal – Duplicative convictions
item.description: Where a jury found a defendant guilty of assault and battery (count one), assault on a family or household member (count two), assault and battery with a dangerous weapon (count three), armed assault in a dwelling (count four) and mayhem (count five), the convictions on counts one and three must be reversed because they are duplicative of count five.

item.title: Zoning – Subdivision rules – Dead-end streets
item.description: Where (1) two plaintiffs filed an application with the planning board of Grafton seeking a special permit and site plan approval to build a multi-family residential development and (2) the board denied waivers from a provision of the town’s subdivision rules imposing length restrictions on dead-end streets, it was arbitrary and capricious to deny the waivers based on alleged safety concerns, so a new judgment should enter directing the board to issue the special permit and site plan review with

item.title: Corporate – Fee award – G.L.c. 156D
item.description: Where (1) a plaintiff brought suit after trying unsuccessfully to get the defendants to provide corporate documents to which she was entitled under G.L.c. 156D and (2) the plaintiff was awarded counsel fees, a remand must be ordered because of the lack of an explanation for the inclusion of fees that appear to fall outside the ambit of the statute.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Website – Purposeful availment
item.description: Where a complaint was filed against a Pennsylvania-based company that owns and operates an online marketplace for firearms and firearm-related products, a U.S. District Court judge’s decision to dismiss the complaint for lack of personal jurisdiction must be vacated in part, as the judge erred in ruling that the plaintiffs failed to establish a prima facie case of purposeful availment.

item.title: Insurance – Beneficiary designation form – FEGLIA
item.description: Where a Postal Service employee insured pursuant to the Federal Employees' Group Life Insurance Act executed a designation form naming the plaintiffs — his ex-wife and his sons — as his beneficiaries, a grant of summary judgment in favor of the plaintiffs should be affirmed because (1) the form met all of the statutory requirements and (2) the employee’s widow failed to demonstrate that he lacked the mental capacity to designate beneficiaries.

item.title: Products liability – Design defect – Warranty of merchantability
item.description: Where a lawsuit was filed after a worker died when a descending steel beam trapped him between two components of a laser-cutting system, a grant of summary judgment in favor of the defendant that designed, sold, installed and maintained the system should be vacated in part, as there is a material factual dispute on whether there was a reasonable alternative design that could have mitigated the system’s dangers.

item.title: Criminal – Double jeopardy
item.description: Where a defendant, following the declaration of a mistrial, has moved motion to dismiss the indictment currently pending against him on double jeopardy grounds, that motion should be allowed because the government has not demonstrated that the mistrial declaration was manifestly necessary.
